title: The Shimmering Puddle
story:
From his high perch on the rocky mound, James looked out across the Whispering Flats. The strange, angular shapes on the horizon did not go away when he blinked. He thought of the Great Canopy where the shadows were soft and green. He thought of the warm boulder where he had sat just days ago. He thought of the metal ring in his hand, cold despite the afternoon sun. Nervous but determined, he closed his eyes to count three distinct sounds. First, he heard the dry whistle of the wind across the flats. Second, he heard the tiny, metallic clink of the ring shifting in his grip. Third, he heard the low, rhythmic thumping of the distant chimney-pipes. Opening his eyes, he whispered to the horizon, "Pleased to meet you, whatever comes next."

Descending the mound was easier than climbing it, though the grey-green dust of the flats rose in small puffs around his feet. As he walked, the metallic scent grew thicker, smelling less like old buried secrets and more like active, living heat. He found himself following a flat, unusually straight strip of hard earth where no weeds grew—a path that seemed to have been laid down on purpose. The further he walked, the more the natural world seemed to bend to someone else's rules.

Eventually, he reached a line of towering, upright wooden posts connected by thin, rusted lines of wire that hummed when the wind caught them. He had never seen trees so perfectly straight. He had never seen vines so sharp. He had never seen a border so clearly drawn. At the foot of one of these posts, he found a small puddle of oily water that shimmered with the colors of a rainbow. He paused to look at his reflection, distorted and wobbling alongside the reflection of the looming human structures in the distance.
location: The Outer Fence of the Whispering Flats
